Response: John, Kate, Jack, and Emma—would you each agree to catch 12 tons this month, with me doing the same? That earns each of us $12,000 instead of $10,000: an extra $2,000 apiece, or $10,000 across the group.

With all five taking 12, we catch 60 tons and leave 40. Under the stated rules, next month’s stock would be 100 tons with 75% probability and 80 tons with 25% probability. Taking 10 each leaves 50, which reaches 100 next month under either outcome. So 12 gives us more income now, but sacrifices that certainty: expected next-month stock is 95 rather than 100 tons. It avoids the collapse threshold if everyone follows the plan, but it is not risk-free or necessarily the best long-run policy.

If your concern is repeating this when stocks are lower, I agree: let’s make this a one-month proposal, not a standing quota. We can reassess after seeing next month’s stock and everyone’s revealed catches. Future cooperation isn’t enforceable, so explicit commitments matter.

I commit to 12 tons this month. Emma, would you support this proposal and commit to 12 too? John, Kate, and Jack, can each of you explicitly agree—or tell us what concern or different whole-ton allocation would earn your agreement?
Conversation conclusion by me: no
Next speaker: Emma
